import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the
accounts API shipped. It uploads to
your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expires

At }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route
creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes\ninto keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in t
he\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored.

Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `details.code` a

re listed in the
[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).

## Run

evals from the API

The shortest useful loop: create a run with one inline test, then poll:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-va
riables\"}\n# 1. Create (responds 202 immediately; -f + jq -e fail fast on errors)\nRUN_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST \\\n \"https://app
.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: ap

tle": "echo works",
 "runs": 1,
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
 "provider": "anthropic",

"id": "s2",
 "kind": "assert",
 "assertion": {
 "type": "toolCalledWith",
m/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 3. If it did not pass, r
ead the decision summary FIRST\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decision-summary\"

\
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"

# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration tool calls, token usage, latency
curl
-s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_AP

I_KEY"
```

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every
client reads a run the same way. F

our things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the
 counts ar
e case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The
same suite reports\n a different total under each, 3 against 15 for three cases run five times,\n so a count without its unit is
not a fact, and a rate is never converted\n across that line.\n* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's
own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it. A case ca
n pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \
"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or
undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision; the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\
n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scan

nedIterations` separates
 "nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a mea
sured failure the span\nids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is

an API-relative path you can append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog (`pr
ovider/name` form, e.g.\n`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`) and runs on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude
-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time w

ith `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "sui
teId\": \"...\" }` reruns the suite exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlis
ts the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_

ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [projec
t environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has\nit **attached**. Attach them first with\n`PATCH /projects/
{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected, use `null`),

then
pass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached
environments; anything else is a `400` with
`deta

ils.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED"`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId
` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:\n\n* **no** attached environments → the run uses the saved server selection, as before;

everal** attached → `400` with `details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.

The environment supplies t
he closed server set, so `serverIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather than accepted and ignored:
honoring\nboth would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfor a `serverIds` override on an environ

ment-based suite
(`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is pinned to the environment revision re
solved at launch: if the\nenvironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT` (409)\nrather than executing against
a different configuration than the one whose\ntools were captured. Use\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/r

esolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a new inline suite, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hos
ts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and optional server selection as `POST .../e
val-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachments, use `namedHostId` to select the run's
client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the run uses the project's default client.\n\
nRun reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }` when recorded. `id` is the named host ID or `n
ull`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The name is durable even if the host is deleted. SDK
executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launching process. Older runs without a descriptor omit
`client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its case snapshot; `client_default` and `override` retain t

heir existing meanings.

Every run records which environment it used. `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` (and
the run listings) return
`environment: { id, name, revision }` (read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot, not the suite's current attachments) or `null` fo

r a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency is capped (default **2** concurrent runs); exceeding

it returns
`429` with `details.reason: "CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT"`; wait for an active run
to finish.

If a server answers `401
OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself\n(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` handles interactive, headless, and\nclient-credenti
als flows) and upload the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-accounts). Subsequent runs inject the stored token, and
